title: Story: Search and filter the current deck and saved decks in GEMP
body:
## User story
As a GEMP deck builder, I want distinct Catalog, Current deck, My decks and Public library search scopes so that I can find cards within a list and find the right saved/published list without confusing those jobs.

## Requirements
- Current-deck filtering highlights/counts existing entries without removing cards or altering the saved list. Preserve quantities and actual zones/setup roles.
- My-decks search covers the signed-in user's authorized records only, with name/card/side/format and available metadata filters. Public library consumes33's public records.
- Clearly label scopes and preserve meaningful navigation/filter context. A catalog match is not proof a card is already in the deck or legal/implemented.
- Reuse public card-filter meanings and exact/family/state handling while keeping private collection/account filters context-specific. Do not index private decks into Wiki or SCOMPLINK.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1 A source/UI audit records current behavior and real saved/current-deck fixture coverage.
- [ ] AC2 A name/symbol/uniqueness query within an open deck returns only appropriate entries/counts, preserves the deck hash and distinguishes no matches from missing metadata.
- [ ] AC3 My-decks and Public library find the expected lists containing a selected card; counts, permissions, exact/family matching and imports are verified.
- [ ] AC4 Existing catalog filtering, editing/saving/import and keyboard/mobile flows pass regression checks.
- [ ] AC5 Tests, native Test/Play verification, backups/rollback, merged source and per-AC PASS support closure.

## Plan/status
Backlog follow-up authorized by Bill14 November2026. Reuse32 public-card parity,33 public library,173 display research and the shared-search pilot. Implement separate scopes incrementally; do not turn the current small public search pilot into a private-data index. Native pilot/appropriate tests before full rollout. Archive.org hold remains intact.
